name: Moszna Castle
architectural_style: A Baroque central palace rebuilt and enlarged after a fire on the night of 2 April 1896, with an eastern neo-Gothic wing and orangery finished by 1900 and a western neo-Renaissance wing added in 1912–1914 — the eclectic mix of towers that gave the estate its popular 'castle of 99 towers' nickname
accessibility: A large estate with a palace building and grounds; contact the hotel directly regarding specific accessibility requirements.
tagline: The Tiele-Winckler family's Silesian industrial-era seat — a Baroque palace rebuilt after an 1896 fire into the eclectic eastern neo-Gothic and western neo-Renaissance wings known as the 'castle of 99 towers' — now a hotel run by the Opole regional authority

A fire on the night of 2 April 1896 partly destroyed the old Baroque central palace

description:
Moszna Castle stands in the village of Moszna in Opole Voivodeship, Upper Silesia, near Prudnik in south-western Poland — an estate whose present, eclectic silhouette is largely the product of a single rebuilding campaign at the turn of the 20th century. From 1866 to 1945 it was the family seat of the Tiele-Winckler family, Silesian industrialists whose wealth shaped the palace's later expansion.

On the night of 2 April 1896, a fire partly destroyed the older Baroque central palace. Franz Hubert von Tiele-Winckler directed the rebuilding and enlargement that followed: an eastern neo-Gothic wing and an orangery were completed by 1900, and a western neo-Renaissance wing was added between 1912 and 1914. The result is a building that mixes several historicist styles under one roofline, with the many towers across its wings giving rise to the estate's popular nickname as the 'castle of 99 towers' — a traditional figure describing the whole building, not a precise architectural count.

After the Second World War, the castle served as a sanatorium. Since 2013 it has been run by the Moszna Zamek company, owned by the regional Marshal's Office of Opole Voivodeship, operating today as a hotel within the historic building while the wider estate remains a visitor attraction in its own right.

Rooms inside the castle are large and simply furnished, several carrying historic names such as the 'Golden Apartment'; one apartment occupies the space where the count's own bedroom once stood.
history: The estate became the family seat of the Silesian industrial Tiele-Winckler family, who held it from 1866 until 1945. A fire on the night of 2 April 1896 partly destroyed the old Baroque central palace; Franz Hubert von Tiele-Winckler then directed the rebuilding and enlargement, with the eastern neo-Gothic wing and an orangery finished by 1900 and the western neo-Renaissance wing built in 1912–1914. After the Second World War it served as a sanatorium; since 2013 it is run by the Moszna Zamek company, owned by the regional (Opole) Marshal's Office.

faqs.question: Can I stay inside Moszna Castle itself?
faqs.answer: Yes — the hotel occupies the historic castle building, with large, simply furnished rooms and apartments, some carrying historic names such as the 'Golden Apartment'.

faqs.question: Does Moszna Castle really have 99 towers and 365 rooms?
faqs.answer: The '99 towers and 365 rooms' figure often quoted for Moszna is a traditional description of the whole castle complex, not an independently verified count, and it refers to the estate as a whole rather than to the hotel's own room count.

faqs.question: Who owns Moszna Castle today?
faqs.answer: Since 2013 it has been run by the Moszna Zamek company, which is owned by the regional Marshal's Office of Opole Voivodeship.

meta_description: Stay at Moszna Castle in Upper Silesia, Poland — the Tiele-Winckler family's eclectic palace, rebuilt after an 1896 fire. Rooms from approx. €123/night.

hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** In the village of Moszna in Opole Voivodeship, in south-western Poland, reached by road; check access and parking with the hotel.

**Rooms & rates:** Large rooms and apartments inside the castle, from approx. €123/night; the cheapest room (30 m², garden view) has a private bathroom that is outside the room, and a Standard Double of 25 m² starts around €143. Rooms are generous in size and simply furnished, with historic names such as 'Golden Apartment'.

**On-site:** Breakfast is included in the rates seen on Booking, along with one parking spot, late check-in and free Wi-Fi in the rooms; no other services are confirmed.

**Good to know:** The '99 towers and 365 rooms' often quoted for Moszna refer to the whole castle, not to the hotel. The estate is a visitor attraction as well as a hotel, so book in advance for weekends.

**Combine with:** The castle park and the building itself, which are the main attraction of the stay.
